lpips_audit.input_handling: Divided by 255 into [0, 1]; passed to LPIPS scaling_layer

clipscore_audit.explanation: In ssr/metrics/clipscore.py, input tensors are only divided by 255 without ImageNet mean and standard deviation normalization. In high-dimensional vision transformer feature spaces, the unnormalized forward pass produces latent vectors clustered in an acute positive hyper-cone (mean feature activation > 0). Consequently, cosine similarity between arbitrary valid natural images is tightly bounded in [0.85, 1.0]. Even severely perturbed images (inverted colors) retain high semantic cosine similarity (~0.9929). Therefore, CLIPScore in this repository must NEVER be interpreted as a percentage quality score, but strictly as a semantic manifold proximity metric where meaningful relative differences occur in the second or third decimal place.
